messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: p99 latency spike > 2s observed for router.euw2 (streaming stalls up x8). Auto-pager triggered. Dashboards: https://dash.company/redwood/routers/euw2/p99. Paging @oncall_robin and eng-runtime.

oncall_robin: acked. joining. what's the scope? any customer impact yet? :eyes:

eng_tariq: looking at traces now. p95 rose to 600ms, p99 > 2s since 18:12 UTC. streaming stalls show a spike in stalled frames on the router layer.

eng_tariq: quick query:
```
index=router_metrics region=euw2 | stats count by route_policy, target_zone | sort - count desc
```
Result: ~40% of requests for policy=balanced-weight-v2 are being routed to target_zone=usw2 (unexpected) — seems like zone skew.

lex_prod: we pushed balanced-weight-v2 ~2h ago to improve cost locality. didn't expect cross-region drift. could be the new hash seed change in that rollout.

maria_sre: can you confirm whether the routing table is honoring zone affinity? I see a lot of rapid reassignments in the logs:
```
2026-03-15T18:13:05Z router[euw2-rt-04]: route assign shard=shard-09 -> zone=usw2 (weight 0.02) previous_zone=euw2
2026-03-15T18:13:06Z router[euw2-rt-07]: route rebalance shard=shard-09 -> zone=usw2
```
This looks like a bug in the weight mixer where small numeric jitter flips the decision and piles traffic onto a subset of backend pools -> hot partition.

jamie_runtime: also seeing connection saturation on gpu-pool-22 in euw2. many streams queueing waiting for CV2 worker availability. p99 tokens wait times show backlog.

eng_tariq: hypothesis: policy balanced-weight-v2 has a bug: when weight differences < 0.05 it occasionally prefers remote zone due to float rounding in the mixer, causing a hot tail on a few pools. reproducing locally.

lex_prod: current proposal: roll back balanced-weight-v2 to balanced-weight-v1 in euw2 immediately, and apply a temporary override to clamp weights for top prefixes. any objections?

maria_sre: +1. mitigation plan (emergency):
1) revert policy to balanced-weight-v1 on all euw2 routers
2) apply weight clamp on router-ingress for prefixes with >1k qps
3) drain gpu-pool-22 and shift traffic to healthy pools
4) open live page & notify customers

oncall_robin: do we have a quick command to revert? I'll run if someone gives me the safe command.

opsbot: executing suggested revert command, please confirm:
```
opsbot run routing set-policy --region euw2 --policy balanced-weight-v1 --selector "env=prod,role=router"
```

lex_prod: confirmed. run it. I'll monitor.

deploy-bot: opsbot: OK: policy set to balanced-weight-v1 on 12/12 routers in euw2. change-id=chg_20260315_001. No errors reported.

maria_sre: applying weight clamp for top prefixes:
```
opsbot run routing override-weights --region euw2 --prefixes-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt --min-weight 0.05
```

opsbot: OK: overrides applied. 26 prefixes updated.

jamie_runtime: starting to drain gpu-pool-22 nodes (graceful). command:
```
kubectl -n runtime drain node/gpu-pool-22-node-3 --timeout=2m --ignore-daemonsets
```

opsbot: drain initiated, pod eviction in progress.

eng_tariq: dashboards show immediate improvement in distribution, p95 dropping to ~250ms. p99 still noisy but trending down.

deploy-bot: after revert + clamp: p99 reduced from ~2.4s -> ~520ms within 6m, streaming stall rate down 70%.

support_jin: customer impact snapshot: 12 customers saw >2s p99 during window 18:12-18:25 UTC. top-affected tenants: tenant-acme, tenant-velox, tenant-boreal (IDs redacted). We're drafting a small incident notice; recommend "brief outage/latency" note with ETA for follow-up after RCA.

oncall_robin: thanks. please add affected customer IDs to the incident ticket. I'll join a quick sync with support to coordinate comms :phone:

maria_sre: next actions:
- keep override in place for 2h while we validate further
- collect routing decision traces for policy balanced-weight-v2 and reproduce locally
- rollback rollout for balanced-weight-v2 globally until fix
- run canary with controlled seed to validate hash determinism

lex_prod: will rollback the rollout flag and pin balanced-weight-v1 for now. filing rollback change chg_20260315_002.

jamie_runtime: will run a slow drain of the remaining nodes and start autoscale on the euw2 gpu pools to absorb load.

eng_tariq: adding trace sample to the incident ticket. I found line in mixer logic where weights < 0.05 are normalized incorrectly — likely the bug.

oncall_robin: livepage open: https://live.redwood/incident/1717668888. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for postmortem. handing off to night oncall at 02:00 UTC — will post handoff notes there.

support_jin: customer comm draft ready, sending to legal + PM for approval. Suggested message: "We observed elevated latency in EU-West2 for streaming requests due to a routing policy regression; services restored after temporary rollback. Root cause analysis will follow." Keep it short.

maria_sre: marking incident as mitigated at 18:34 UTC. continuing monitoring. assigning postmortem to eng_tariq + lex_prod. cc: support_jin for customer notes.

eng_tariq: I'll include repro steps, stack trace, and affected prefix list in the postmortem. plan to propose a unit test and float comparison fix.

oncall_robin: thanks team. leaving notes for handoff: mitigation performed (policy revert + weight clamp + drain), customers notified, livepage + ticket updated. handing off to night oncall @oncall_sam at 02:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

opsbot: incident closed to active mitigation channel; monitoring continues for 24h. auto-escalate if p99 > 1s again.

incident-bot: :ticket: Incident ticket #INC-20260315-1717668888 created. postmortem owners: eng_tariq, lex_prod, maria_sre.

support_jin: will follow up with affected customers tomorrow with more details and next steps.

jamie_runtime: leaving a note to run a targeted canary with a fixed hash seed tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

maria_sre: end of thread summary: root cause = routing weight normalization bug in balanced-weight-v2; impact = p99 latency spikes and streaming stalls due to hotspotting; mitigation = rollback to balanced-weight-v1, weight clamp, drain of saturated pool. next steps = rollback rollout, fix mixer float handling, add unit + e2e tests, coordinated canary.

oncall_robin: acknowledged. I'll update the incident ticket and schedule the postmortem sync for tomorrow 11:00 UTC. :calendar:
